The restrictions will affect commuters travelling between Hebbal, central Bengaluru and Kempegowda International Airport (KIA). The Bengaluru Traffic Police have prohibited all goods vehicles, including light, medium and heavy goods vehicles, as well as KSRTC and private buses, from using the affected stretch. Cars, two-wheelers and school buses can continue to use the road. The four-lane elevated corridor will run between the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS) staff quarters and Mehkri Circle, covering around 1.6 km. The stretch falls under the jurisdiction of the Sadashivanagar and Sanjaynagar traffic police stations. The construction is expected to take 18 months. The corridor is part of the BDA’s Rs 2,215-crore project to ease congestion at the Hebbal junction. The Court explained that the rule introduced a restriction that did not previously exist and could therefore operate only from the date it came into force.
